The commit being fixed was aiming to disallow users from incorrectly
obtaining writable pointer to memory that is only meant to be read. This
is enforced now using a MEM_RDONLY flag.

column2: in case of global percpu variables
the verifier marks register type as

column1: PTR_TO_MEM | MEM_RDONLY from bpf_this_cpu_ptr or bpf_per_cpu_ptr

column2: when passing such pointer to kfunc
hence it is checked as pointer to writable
verifier sets up argument type of global func as
so user can use a global func to get around

column1: the limitations imposed by this flag.
This check will also cover global non-percpu variables that may be
introduced in kernel BTF in future.

column2: we update the log message for PTR_TO_BUF case to be similar to
so that the reason for error is clear to user.
